drivers.text: Azure grew 48% on demand across the platform with growth across all workloads; Microsoft 365 commercial cloud up 17% on higher revenue per user (Copilot, E5, E7 upsell) and usage-based services such as GitHub Copilot.
Agents and Infra cost of revenue up 35% on datacenter infrastructure investment to support Azure and Microsoft 365 cloud demand.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage fell to 66% on mix shift toward Azure, partly offset by product-level margin gains primarily in Azure.
Investing outflow rose mainly from a $20.0 billion increase in additions to property and equipment, plus higher other investing to facilitate component purchases.
Devices and Consumer revenue fell 3%, with Windows OEM and devices down 22% on lapping Windows 10 end-of-support demand, OEM/channel inventory drawdowns and weaker PC demand.

gaps: Microsoft no longer reports an Intelligent Cloud segment from FY27 (segments recast to Agents and Infra and Devices and Consumer; announced Sept 2026). Agents and Infra includes Microsoft 365 cloud and other lines, so it is not a like-for-like Intelligent Cloud figure. The FY2026 10-K still reports Intelligent Cloud (annual only).
capex_guidance: the release says guidance is given on the call (line 52); no capex figure in the filings.

capex_incl_finance_leases_q: no single disclosed figure; inputs are additions to PP&E 39,367, finance-lease ROU assets obtained 5,192, and financing cash flows from finance leases 1,000. Accounts-payable-accrued PP&E is 26.5 billion at 2026-09-30 (10-Q line 603).
useful_life_change: no change in estimated useful lives found in the FY2026 10-K or Q1 FY27 10-Q text searched; the 10-K states only the 2-to-6-year servers range.
Microsoft Cloud prior-year (49.1) and several RPO and lease figures sit on lines of their own in the 10-Q, so quotes are bare numbers (billions).
Headcount: the 10-Q says total company headcount decreased 2% (line 1074) but gives no 10-Q count.
